stem: The halogens, chlorine, bromine and iodine, and their compounds, show a variety of similarities and trends in their physical and chemical properties.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Give the colours and states of chlorine, bromine and iodine at room temperature and pressure.

| halogen | colour | state |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| chlorine |  |  |
| bromine |  |  |
| iodine |  |  |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The halogens become less volatile down the group.

Explain this trend in volatility.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The halogens are oxidising agents.

State and explain the trend in oxidising power of the halogens.

parts.text: State any observations that would be made on addition of concentrated sulfuric acid to

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Give reasons for the difference in the observations in (i).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The addition of concentrated sulfuric acid to solid sodium bromide, $\text{NaBr}$, produces brown fumes and an acidic gas that decolourises acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution. This acidic gas is a significant contributor to acid rain.

Write the equation for the reaction of concentrated sulfuric acid with sodium bromide.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: An aqueous solution, $\mathbf{Z}$, contains a mixture of sodium chloride and sodium iodide.
parts.text:
Excess aqueous silver nitrate is added to $\mathbf{Z}$ in a test-tube. A yellow precipitate forms.

Explain the colour of this precipitate.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Aqueous ammonia is then added to the test-tube in (i). The mass of precipitate decreases.

Explain this observation.
